title: Revamp button interaction patterns: loading UX, icon alignment, and theme token gaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket covers a focused revamp of button interaction patterns across the design system. Goals are to: 1) standardize loading and disabled affordances across primary/secondary/ghost variants; 2) fix inconsistent icon spacing and vertical alignment for icon+label and icon-only buttons; 3) fill missing theme tokens that produce color regressions in dark mode and high-contrast themes.

Background & motivation:
Over the last two releases we shipped variant changes and motion updates which unintentionally diverged token usage between the React component, CSS tokens, and Figma styles. This resulted in a class of visual regressions (tertiary/ghost borders disappearing in dark mode), inconsistent spinner scaling, and a handful of accessibility reports around focus ring visibility when buttons are loading.

Scope (what we'll do in this ticket):
- Audit existing button tokens in Figma, CSS and runtime (component props) and produce a canonical token map.
- Define explicit loading states for each variant: spinner size, mute/opaque label behavior, disabled pointer events, announced accessible label (aria-live guidance).
- Rework icon spacing rules: 16px baseline for icon+label gap (adjusted to visual optically 14px on compact), 12px for icon-only touch targets where applicable.
- Add missing theme tokens: button-border-weak, button-bg-elevated, button-loading-contrast to bridge desktop/dark/high-contrast themes.
- Provide a backward-compatible tokens shim and a migration guide for engineering (see attachments).
- Create visual QA checklist (light/dark/contrast/embedded UIs) and automated Percy snapshots for primary flows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Documentation: token map published in Design System docs and Figma component library updated.
- Component: React button uses new tokens behind a feature flag; no visual diffs for baseline tests but fixes previously observed regressions in dark mode.
- Accessibility: screen reader announces "Loading" when button enters loading state and keyboard focus visible in all modes.
- Engineering: ENG-2122 implements token mapping and ENG-2199 adds Percy snapshots.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Spinner vs skeleton: we standardize on a compact spinner for transient actions (<2s) and recommend skeletons for longer loads. This keeps complexity lower in the component but requires consuming teams to opt into skeletons when appropriate.
- Token naming: we chose actionable names (button-border-weak) over semantic-only names to make mapping to CSS variables explicit. This increases churn at first but reduces ambiguity for engineers.
- Feature flag rollout: we'll gate visual token switch behind design-system-2.14 to allow stepwise PRs and smaller visual review windows.

Links & artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Redwood-Buttons (prototype & token page)
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Button+Interaction+Revamp
- Engineering PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/378
- Percy baseline: https://percy.io/redwood/buttons/changesets/10321
comments: 2025-02-11 — Aisha: Initial audit completed, attached token spreadsheet in Confluence. Observed 6 mismatched tokens across Figma/CSS/runtime.
2025-02-12 — Marco: Dropped first dev spike note. ENG-2122 to add runtime token mapping; identified compatibility risk with older consumers using inline styles.

2025-02-14 — Design review: PM and Accessibility reviewed. PM asked we preserve existing micro-interaction timing where possible. Accessibility requested explicit aria-label guidelines for loading buttons.
2025-02-16 — Marco: Prototype PR opened (feature-flagged). Spinner scaled to 14px for compact and 18px for default. Noted one failing Percy snapshot in dark ghost variant.
2025-02-18 — Aisha: Resolved dark ghost border by introducing button-border-weak token. Updated spec and added migration notes for ENG-2199. Marking for review with engineering and QA next.
2025-02-18 — QA: Added visual QA checklist to attachments and scheduled cross-team visual review on 2025-02-20.
